sampling_model.design: Complete randomization draws \(W\) uniformly from assignments with exactly \(m\) treated units; the design variable includes the integer \(m\) and the common local channel \(Q\).
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) labeled units and both binary potential outcomes are fixed; there is no superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The private input \((W_i,Y_i(W_i))\) belongs to \(\mathcal X\), and the analyst does not separately observe \(W_i\) or \(Y_i(W_i)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The treatment count obeys \(1\le m<N\); no propensity model is estimated.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The nuisance is the full finite schedule orbit \(n\in\mathcal O_N\); inference imposes coverage for every orbit and does not estimate a superpopulation regression.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A finite family of extremal mechanisms, which we call staircase mechanisms, contains the optimal privatization mechanism.
Using a customized privacy mechanism, we can match the lower bound, giving minimax optimal inference.
Both of the resulting \(1-\alpha\) confidence sets are exact.
Inverting the likelihood ratio test minimizes the probability of including false values in the confidence region.
The same non-asymptotic confidence intervals hold for the sample average treatment effect.
We provide a sequence of values, returned by semidefinite programs, finitely converges to the minimal value.
Every extreme point of the fixed-output joint range is attained by a sort--partition--randomize mechanism.

body.tldr: Exact finite-population SATE inference under local privacy reduces to a fourteen-pattern, degree-\(N\) polynomial channel game with an inner exact confidence linear program. At \(N=4\), \(\alpha=2/5\), and \(\lambda=1000\), rational certificates bracket the unrestricted optimum within \(5.94\times10^{-6}\), while revealed-input dominance and monotone privacy feasibility force balanced allocation for every \(\lambda\ge1000\). Four-ary response strictly beats every balanced binary-partition response throughout \([999.9,1000.1]\). No optimizer-attaining balanced-binary cell or actual equality-set boundary is established.

project_justification.gap: Existing causal local-privacy theory optimizes population estimation risk or asymptotic confidence width, exact randomization inference fixes a nonprivate observation experiment, and staircase optimality applies to convex single-draw utilities. Their intersection leaves the exact common-channel SATE confidence game and its design boundaries unresolved.
project_justification.niche: The finite binary schedule, complete-randomization orbit structure, and four protected input values make the causal nuisance finite while preserving the nonconvex product-channel difficulty.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a lossless schedule-orbit reduction, an explicit fourteen-output Blackwell refinement, exact fixed-channel primal--dual confidence inference, an attained degree-\(N\) polynomial formulation, a global polynomial-dual certificate method, a certified nonbinary interval, and a balanced-allocation theorem for the stated four-unit regime. It does not claim the previously proposed balanced-binary phase boundary, whose optimizer-attaining certificate remains open.

body.related_work: Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath (2016), Section 7 and Lemma 22, provide the cube decomposition underlying the staircase factorization of a pure locally private column. The present reduction uses that geometric basis and adds the problem-specific strengthening: it explicitly absorbs the constant ray into complementary nonconstant patterns, normalizes the resulting fourteen weights, extracts an input-independent postprocessing kernel, and thereby obtains Blackwell dominance for the entire finite-population confidence game. Their convex-utility output-size conclusions do not apply because the optimized product-channel confidence utility is not convex in the required direction. Ohnishi and Awan (2025) study locally private causal inference for a superpopulation PATE under Bernoulli treatment and asymptotic estimation or inference; the present target is the fixed-population SATE under complete randomization with a hidden assignment. Rigdon and Hudgens (2015) treat exact finite-population SATE inference without this local channel-design game. Schafer and Stark (2009) motivate least-favorable-prior confidence optimization for a fixed experiment. Chen, Cormode, Bharadwaj, Romov, and Ozgur (2024) optimize distributed-private mechanisms and allocation but do not derive this schedulewise exact common-channel game or its boundaries. Ghazi, Nasser, Calmon, and Issa (2026) obtain partition mechanisms for simple binary testing, whereas the current confidence problem has many schedule nulls and no single likelihood-ratio ordering.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact unrestricted lower certificate at \((N,\alpha,\lambda)=(4,2/5,1000)\) misses the feasible upper value by \(297/50000000\). This positive slack is small enough for the stated value bracket but prevents identification of a minimizing channel. The checked balanced-binary fixed-channel duals also fail to yield a matching lower bound over the full staircase polytope. Consequently there is no equality identity to continue, and no certified two-dimensional cell, frontier polynomial, isolating interval, sign change of \(\Delta_{4,\alpha}(\lambda)\), or channel-support or confidence-basis transition has been obtained.
body.honest_scope: The proved contribution consists of the exact orbit kernel, fourteen-output Blackwell refinement, fixed-channel primal--dual program, attained polynomial formulation, nonconvexity witness, global positive-tolerance bracket, balanced allocation for \(N=4\), \(\alpha=2/5\), and every \(\lambda\ge1000\), and the nonbinary exclusion interval \([999.9,1000.1]\). The certificate-characterization theorem remains conditional: it explains how an explicitly supplied attaining family would certify a cell and boundary, but no such family is supplied. In particular, the paper does not claim a nonempty balanced-binary equality cell, an endpoint polynomial, an isolated root, a sign-certified phase transition, four-output sufficiency, general-\(N\) balance, or a practical advantage at conventional coverage. Consumer use requires a hidden-assignment protocol in which the analyst observes only privatized reports and the known design quantities.
body.interpretation: The two-parameter equality locus consists of pairs \((\lambda,\alpha)\) satisfying \(\lambda\in\mathcal B_{N,\alpha}\). For a fixed \(\alpha\), the set \(\mathcal B_{N,\alpha}\subset(1,\infty)\) is only the horizontal section of that locus, and an endpoint is a one-dimensional section boundary. A two-dimensional optimizer cell would have to be proved before a transverse fixed-\(\alpha\) root could be called an actual phase boundary. The current certificates instead identify a two-sided exclusion interval in one fixed section.
